source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the bustling terminal, a long queue snaked towards the security checkpoint. Items were methodically laid out on conveyor belts, each piece scanned through clear glass. Metal detectors beeped as travelers passed, and when the alarm sounded, a detailed pat-down was conducted. At a certain point, an officer singled out a traveler from the line, asking to see identification and boarding passes. The traveler stepped aside, their belongings held momentarily. The officer then moved closer, inspecting the traveler’s bag and conducting a thorough search. Instructions were displayed on screens, guiding everyone through the process, with clear signs directing traffic and ensuring a steady flow. The authority was impersonal but firm, maintaining order amidst the constant stream of people.

At the bustling airport checkpoint, a queue snaked through the barriers where travelers laid their belongings on trays. The scanners hissed, and metal detectors beeped, while officers conducted body searches. Amidst the stream, an officer flagged down a traveler, inspecting her documents and conducting a thorough pat-down. Signs and instructions lined the walls, offering clear guidance, while the officer maintained a formal, impersonal demeanor.

At the bustling checkpoint, a queue snaked past the barriers where travelers laid their belongings in trays. The scanners hummed softly, and the metal detectors beeped sharply. An officer, motioning for someone to step forward, singled them out from the line. They presented their documents, and after a thorough pat-down, they were allowed to proceed.

In the background, instructions were clearly posted, and signs directed passengers through various stages. The officer, though stern in demeanor, was courteous in his interaction, embodying the impersonal yet necessary register of control.

At the terminal, amidst a crowd, a line stretched long behind a barrier. Belongings were passed through trays, each item laid bare. Scanners hummed silently, while metal detectors buzzed with travelers passing through. An officer paused, his gaze drawn to a single traveler, who stepped forward from the queue. Documents were inspected, and a gentle pat-down followed, a routine motion that seemed almost ritualistic. Instructions hung above, clear and concise, while signs pointed directions. The air was thick with the impersonal courtesy of authority, a necessary register of control. Numbers moved in sequence, each traveler’s passage marked by a series of checks and balances. The officer returned to the line, his eyes scanning again, ensuring all was in order. Documents were rechecked, and belongings scanned once more, the process a cycle of thoroughness and efficiency. The line continued to move, each traveler subjected to the same meticulous scrutiny, a reminder of the vigilant watchfulness required in these busy hours.

In the bustling queue, bags were placed on trays, awaiting inspection. Along the barrier, items were carefully laid out for the scanners. Nearby, metal detectors hummed, and officers gestured travellers to remove clothing for a thorough pat-down. Among the queue, two individuals were singled out—papers and a pat-down were conducted under the watchful eye of the security officer. On the wall, signs instructed and regulated the process, maintaining the impersonal yet necessary courtesy of authority.

At the bustling checkpoint, the queue snaked through the barriers, each traveler divesting their belongings into trays. The scanners hissed, their green lights scanning through the contents. Metal detectors beeped, and officers gestured travelers to step aside for a more thorough search. Amongst them, a traveler was singled out; their documents were checked, followed by a pat-down with the wand. Signs and instructions lined the walls, their impersonal courtesy stark and unwavering. "Please place your laptop on the tray," "Wait behind the yellow line," and "All passengers proceed." The officer's voice echoed over the intercom, clear and authoritative.

In the bustling queue, marked by a sign saying "security," a traveler's bag slid onto a conveyor belt. The metal detector whistled sharply as he walked through, and the officer motioned him to the side. Documents were laid out on a tray, and a thorough pat-down began, with a polite but firm touch. Above, a screen displayed a list of prohibited items, and a speaker repeated instructions: "Please remove all electronics and liquids from your bags." The officer scanned each item, noting them against a registry. Nearby, a sign read "for your safety," and another, "please cooperate." The traveler felt the cold metal of the scanner and the gentle pressure of the officer's hand as they moved across his body.
